postTitle: One Income, No Backup: Planning for a Household of One
topic: On one income, savings cover the whole of the monthly bills when pay stops

assumptions.notes: Reel's own example, illustrative: €2,400 of monthly bills; with no other income savings cover all of it; with another income of €1,200 they cover half, so the same fund lasts twice as long. The lesson's example: a single earner's fund lasts 6 months, a couple's nearly 20.

caption.instagram:
Your monthly bills are €2,400. If your pay stops, what comes from savings?

On one income, all of it. In a household where another income still pays €1,200, savings cover only the other €1,200, so the same fund lasts twice as long.

That second income sits quietly inside the common rule of three to six months of spending. In the lesson's example a couple's six month fund lasts nearly 20 months after one job is lost, and a single earner's lasts six. On one income, many people aim for the upper end or beyond, often six to twelve months, depending on how steady the income is and how long new work would take to find.
